claim: Sympathetic denervation of the heart following ischemia/reperfusion induced myocardial infarction (MI) is sustained by chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans (CSPGs) in the cardiac scar.
source: Sympathetic denervation of the heart following ischemia/reperfusion induced myocardial infarction (MI) is sustained by chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans (CSPGs) in the cardiac scar.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about the mechanism of denervation.

claim: Denervation predicts risk of sudden cardiac death in humans.
source: Denervation predicts risk of sudden cardiac death in humans.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Blocking CSPG signaling restores sympathetic axon outgrowth into the cardiac scar, decreasing arrhythmia susceptibility.
source: Blocking CSPG signaling restores sympathetic axon outgrowth into the cardiac scar, decreasing arrhythmia susceptibility.
evidence: This is stated as a known effect in the abstract.

claim: Axon growth inhibition by CSPGs can depend on the sulfation status of the glycosaminoglycan (CS-GAG) side chains.
source: Axon growth inhibition by CSPGs can depend on the sulfation status of the glycosaminoglycan (CS-GAG) side chains.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Tandem sulfation of CS-GAGs at the 4th (4S) and 6th (6S) positions of n-acetyl-galactosamine inhibits outgrowth in several types of central neurons.
source: Tandem sulfation of CS-GAGs at the 4th (4S) and 6th (6S) positions of n-acetyl-galactosamine inhibits outgrowth in several types of central neurons, but we don't know if sulfation is similarly critical during peripheral nerve regeneration.
evidence: This is stated as known information about central neurons in the abstract.

claim: Reducing 4S with the 4-sulfatase enzyme Arylsulfatase-B (ARSB) enhanced outgrowth of dissociated rat sympathetic neurons over CSPGs.
source: Reducing 4S with the 4-sulfatase enzyme Arylsulfatase-B (ARSB) enhanced outgrowth of dissociated rat sympathetic neurons over CSPGs.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 2.

claim: Reducing 4S with ARSB restored axon outgrowth from mouse sympathetic ganglia co-cultured with cardiac scar tissue.
source: Likewise, reducing 4S with ARSB restored axon outgrowth from mouse sympathetic ganglia co-cultured with cardiac scar tissue.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: CHST15 (4S dependent 6-sulfotransferase) was upregulated after MI.
source: We quantified enzymes responsible for adding and removing sulfation, and found that CHST15 (4S dependent 6-sulfotransferase) was upregulated, and ARSB was downregulated after MI.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: ARSB was downregulated after MI.
source: We quantified enzymes responsible for adding and removing sulfation, and found that CHST15 (4S dependent 6-sulfotransferase) was upregulated, and ARSB was downregulated after MI.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: Transient siRNA knockdown of Chst15 after MI decreased 4S,6S CS-GAGs in vivo.
source: We decreased 4S,6S CS-GAGs in vivo by transient siRNA knockdown of Chst15 after MI, and found that reducing 4S,6S restored tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) positive sympathetic nerve fibers in the cardiac scar.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: Reducing 4S,6S by Chst15 knockdown restored tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) positive sympathetic nerve fibers in the cardiac scar.
source: We decreased 4S,6S CS-GAGs in vivo by transient siRNA knockdown of Chst15 after MI, and found that reducing 4S,6S restored tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) positive sympathetic nerve fibers in the cardiac scar.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: Reinnervation reduced isoproterenol induced arrhythmias.
source: Reinnervation reduced isoproterenol induced arrhythmias.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 7F.

claim: Sympathetic denervation following myocardial infarction (MI) is well documented in both animal models and humans.
source: Sympathetic denervation following myocardial infarction (MI) is well documented in both animal models and humans, and highly predictive of ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death (Boogers et al., 2010; Fallavollita et al., 2014; Nishisato et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Sympathetic denervation is highly predictive of ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death.
source: Sympathetic denervation following myocardial infarction (MI) is well documented in both animal models and humans, and highly predictive of ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death (Boogers et al., 2010; Fallavollita et al., 2014; Nishisato et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Following an early period of axon degeneration after MI caused by ischemia/reperfusion (I/R), sympathetic nerves grow back through undamaged myocardium but do not enter the scar due to the presence of chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans (CSPGs).
source: Following an early period of axon degeneration after MI caused by ischemia/reperfusion (I/R), sympathetic nerves grow back through undamaged myocardium but do not enter the scar due to the presence of chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans (CSPGs) (Gardner and Habecker, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Heterogeneity in sympathetic innervation increases risk for arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death.
source: This heterogeneity in sympathetic innervation increases risk for arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death (Herring et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: CSPGs are a diverse family of extracellular matrix proteins modified by chondroitin sulfate (CS) side chains that inhibit nerve regeneration in numerous injury paradigms including MI, spinal cord injury (SCI), and traumatic brain injury (TBI).
source: CSPGs are a diverse family of extracellular matrix proteins modified by chondroitin sulfate (CS) side chains that inhibit nerve regeneration in numerous injury paradigms including MI, spinal cord injury (SCI), and traumatic brain injury (TBI) (Brown et al., 2012; Gardner and Habecker, 2013; Lang et al., 2015; McKeon et al., 1999; Miller and Hsieh-Wilson, 2015; Yi et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: CSPGs are heterogeneous but all are composed of a core protein that is covalently linked to repeating disaccharide side chains known as glycosaminoglycans (GAGs).
source: CSPGs are heterogeneous but all are composed of a core protein that is covalently linked to repeating disaccharide side chains known as glycosaminoglycans (GAGs).
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about CSPG structure.

claim: Some evidence suggests that the CSPG core protein itself plays a role in regulating axon outgrowth.
source: While some evidence suggests that the CSPG core protein itself plays a role in regulating axon outgrowth (Dou and Levine, 1994; Ughrin et al., 2003), the primary effect is thought to occur via the post-translational addition of sulfate to GAGs (Mencio et al., 2021; Miller and Hsieh-Wilson, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The primary effect of CSPGs on axon outgrowth is thought to occur via the post-translational addition of sulfate to GAGs.
source: While some evidence suggests that the CSPG core protein itself plays a role in regulating axon outgrowth (Dou and Levine, 1994; Ughrin et al., 2003), the primary effect is thought to occur via the post-translational addition of sulfate to GAGs (Mencio et al., 2021; Miller and Hsieh-Wilson, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: CS-GAGs in scar tissues bind CSPG receptors like PTPσ (protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor sigma) on regenerating axons.
source: CS-GAGs in scar tissues bind CSPG receptors like PTPσ (protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor sigma) on regenerating axons (Coles et al., 2011; Shen et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: CSPG sulfation is attached to specific locations of the CS-GAG by sulfotransferase enzymes, yielding unique structures that differentially affect axon outgrowth.
source: CSPG sulfation is attached to specific locations of the CS-GAG by sulfotransferase enzymes, yielding unique structures that differentially affect axon outgrowth.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about CSPG sulfation.

claim: 4-sulfation (4S) and 6-sulfation (6S) of N-acetyl-galactosamine are critical regulators of axon outgrowth.
source: Specifically, 4-sulfation (4S) and 6-sulfation (6S) of N-acetyl-galactosamine are critical regulators of axon outgrowth (Brown et al., 2012; Gilbert et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: 4S CS-GAGs are produced by the chondroitin-4-sulfotransferase, CHST11.
source: 4S CS-GAGs are produced by the chondroitin-4-sulfotransferase, CHST11, while 4,6-tandem sulfated GAGs (4S,6S) are produced by a 4S-dependent chondroitin-6-sulfotransferase, CHST15 (Miller and Hsieh-Wilson, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: 4,6-tandem sulfated GAGs (4S,6S) are produced by a 4S-dependent chondroitin-6-sulfotransferase, CHST15.
source: 4S CS-GAGs are produced by the chondroitin-4-sulfotransferase, CHST11, while 4,6-tandem sulfated GAGs (4S,6S) are produced by a 4S-dependent chondroitin-6-sulfotransferase, CHST15 (Miller and Hsieh-Wilson, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: 4S CS-GAGs can be removed by an endogenously expressed 4-sulfatase, arylsulfatase-B (ARSB).
source: 4S CS-GAGs can also be removed by an endogenously expressed 4-sulfatase, arylsulfatase-B (ARSB) (Figure 1A; Pearson et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Evidence from SCI and TBI indicate that tandem sulfated 4S,6S CS-GAGs potently suppress axon outgrowth.
source: Evidence from SCI and TBI indicate that tandem sulfated 4S,6S CS-GAGs potently suppress axon outgrowth (Brown et al., 2012; Gilbert et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Removal of all CS-GAGs from cardiac scar tissue by treatment with the enzyme chondroitinase ABC (chABC) restores sympathetic axon outgrowth in vitro.
source: Removal of all CS-GAGs from cardiac scar tissue by treatment with the enzyme chondroitinase ABC (chABC) restores sympathetic axon outgrowth in vitro (Gardner and Habecker, 2013) but it remains unknown whether CSPG sulfation is critical to inhibit regeneration of peripheral nerves.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: 4-Sulfation (4S CS-GAGs) increased in the cardiac scar 14 days after MI compared to healthy myocardium.
source: (B) 4-Sulfation (4S CS-GAGs) or (C) 6-sulfation (6S CS-GAGs) quantification assessed by western blot in the healthy myocardium (unoperated) or cardiac scar 14 days after MI (MI). Quantification of n=6 animals per treatment group, mean optical density (OD) ± SD, Student's t-test (Welch's test), 4S ****p-value < 0 .0001, 6S **p-value = 0.003.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1B-D with statistical analysis.

claim: 6-Sulfation (6S CS-GAGs) increased in the cardiac scar 14 days after MI compared to healthy myocardium.
source: (B) 4-Sulfation (4S CS-GAGs) or (C) 6-sulfation (6S CS-GAGs) quantification assessed by western blot in the healthy myocardium (unoperated) or cardiac scar 14 days after MI (MI). Quantification of n=6 animals per treatment group, mean optical density (OD) ± SD, Student's t-test (Welch's test), 4S ****p-value < 0 .0001, 6S **p-value = 0.003.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1B-D with statistical analysis.

claim: I/R led to increased 4,6-sulfation of CSPGs in the cardiac scar.
source: I/R led to increased 4,6-sulfation of CSPGs in the cardiac scar (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1B-D.

claim: CSPG levels are low in remote myocardium.
source: In contrast, CSPG levels are low in remote myocardium (Gardner and Habecker, 2013), and 4S is not altered after I/R (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: 4S is not altered in remote myocardium after I/R.
source: In contrast, CSPG levels are low in remote myocardium (Gardner and Habecker, 2013), and 4S is not altered after I/R (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Sympathetic neurite extension across untreated CSPGs was suppressed 40 hr post-plating compared to laminin alone.
source: Sympathetic neurite extension across untreated CSPGs was suppressed 40 hr post-plating compared to laminin alone, while ARSB treatment restored neurite outgrowth in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: ARSB treatment restored neurite outgrowth in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Sympathetic neurite extension across untreated CSPGs was suppressed 40 hr post-plating compared to laminin alone, while ARSB treatment restored neurite outgrowth in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: 4S of CS-GAGs inhibits sympathetic neurite extension.
source: These results indicate that 4S of CS-GAGs inhibits sympathetic neurite extension.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results showing that ARSB (which removes 4S) restores neurite outgrowth.

claim: SCG explants co-cultured with unoperated left ventricle displayed uniform axon outgrowth in all directions.
source: Ganglion explants co-cultured with unoperated left ventricle displayed uniform axon outgrowth in all directions while explants cultured alongside cardiac scar tissue (10–14 days post-I/R) exhibited shorter axons growing in the direction of the scar tissue (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B-D.

claim: Explants cultured alongside cardiac scar tissue (10–14 days post-I/R) exhibited shorter axons growing in the direction of the scar tissue.
source: Ganglion explants co-cultured with unoperated left ventricle displayed uniform axon outgrowth in all directions while explants cultured alongside cardiac scar tissue (10–14 days post-I/R) exhibited shorter axons growing in the direction of the scar tissue (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B-D.

claim: ARSB treatment (0.6 µg/mL) of scar tissue fully restored axon outgrowth towards the scar.
source: Interestingly, ARSB treatment (0.6 µg/mL) of scar tissue fully restored axon outgrowth towards the scar (Figure 3D), while growth away from the scar tissue was normal in all conditions (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Growth away from the scar tissue was normal in all conditions.
source: Interestingly, ARSB treatment (0.6 µg/mL) of scar tissue fully restored axon outgrowth towards the scar (Figure 3D), while growth away from the scar tissue was normal in all conditions (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: ARSB treatment of control explants had no effect on axon outgrowth.
source: ARSB treatment of control explants had no effect on axon outgrowth, suggesting its effects are through altering the cardiac scar rather than the ganglion.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the explant co-culture experiments.

claim: Reducing 4S of CS-GAGs in the cardiac scar is sufficient to enable sympathetic axon regeneration.
source: Together, these data suggest that reducing 4S of CS-GAGs in the cardiac scar is sufficient to enable sympathetic axon regeneration.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results with ARSB treatment.

claim: CHST11 levels decreased significantly within 24 hr after MI, persisting until day 7.
source: CHST11 levels decreased significantly within 24 hr, persisting until day 7 (Figure 4A and D), while CHST15 was increased significantly at days 7 and 14 post-MI (Figure 4B and D).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4A and D with statistical analysis.

claim: CHST15 was increased significantly at days 7 and 14 post-MI.
source: CHST11 levels decreased significantly within 24 hr, persisting until day 7 (Figure 4A and D), while CHST15 was increased significantly at days 7 and 14 post-MI (Figure 4B and D).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4B and D with statistical analysis.

claim: ARSB levels decreased significantly by day 3 and remained low through day 14 after MI.
source: ARSB levels decreased significantly by day 3 and remained low through day 14 (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4C and D with statistical analysis.

claim: 4S CS-GAGs are significantly increased in the infarct by day 7 post-MI extending through day 14.
source: 4S and 6S CS-GAGs are significantly increased in the infarct by day 7 post-MI extending through day 14 (Figure 5A, B and E).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5A, B and E with statistical analysis.

claim: 6S CS-GAGs are significantly increased in the infarct by day 7 post-MI extending through day 14.
source: 4S and 6S CS-GAGs are significantly increased in the infarct by day 7 post-MI extending through day 14 (Figure 5A, B and E).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5A, B and E with statistical analysis.

claim: NG2 was increased in the infarct by 7 days after MI.
source: We asked if the CSPG core protein NG2 (also called CSPG4) was also altered after I/R, and found that NG2 was increased in the infarct by 7 days after MI (Figure 5C and E).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5C and E with statistical analysis.

claim: Core proteins and sulfation of CS-GAG side chains are both in greater abundance after MI.
source: Thus, core proteins and sulfation of CS-GAG side chains are both in greater abundance.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing increased NG2 and increased sulfation.

claim: NG2 was prominently expressed in a recent glycoproteomics analysis of cardiac scar tissue.
source: We chose to look at NG2 because it was prominently expressed in a recent glycoproteomics analysis of cardiac scar tissue whereas another commonly studied core proteoglycan, Aggrecan, was not detected (Tian et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Aggrecan was not detected in a recent glycoproteomics analysis of cardiac scar tissue.
source: We chose to look at NG2 because it was prominently expressed in a recent glycoproteomics analysis of cardiac scar tissue whereas another commonly studied core proteoglycan, Aggrecan, was not detected (Tian et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Galectin-3 has been connected to CSPG sulfation and ARSB expression.
source: In an effort to better understand how this process may be coordinated, we examined the expression of a key wound healing regulator, Galectin-3, which has also been connected to CSPG sulfation and ARSB expression (Bhattacharyya et al., 2020; Bhattacharyya et al., 2017; Bhattacharyya et al., 2014; Bhattacharyya et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Galectin-3 was increased significantly by 24 hr after I/R.
source: Galectin-3 was increased significantly by 24 hr after I/R, which may contribute to altered expression of CSPG sulfation enzymes at later time points (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5D and E with statistical analysis.

claim: Increased Galectin-3 may contribute to altered expression of CSPG sulfation enzymes at later time points.
source: Galectin-3 was increased significantly by 24 hr after I/R, which may contribute to altered expression of CSPG sulfation enzymes at later time points (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential role of Galectin-3.

claim: Increased CHST15 and decreased ARSB expression contribute to increased 4,6-sulfation of CS-GAGs observed by day 7 post-MI.
source: These data suggest that increased CHST15 and decreased ARSB expression contribute to increased 4,6-sulfation of CS-GAGs observed by day 7 post-MI.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the temporal correlation of enzyme expression changes and sulfation changes.

claim: Intravenous delivery of 100 µg siChst15 reduced CHST15 protein compared to non-targeting control siRNA.
source: Intravenous delivery of 100 µg siChst15 reduced CHST15 protein compared to non-targeting control siRNA (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: siChst15 reduced the amount of 6S present 10 days post-MI compared to non-targeting siRNA control.
source: Mice were then treated with 100 µg siChst15 on days 3, 5, and 7 post-MI, leading to a significant reduction in 4S,6S CS-GAGs. Specifically, siChst15 reduced the amount of 6S present 10 days post-MI compared to non-targeting siRNA control (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6A with statistical analysis.

claim: By 10 days after MI, CHST15 protein levels had returned to normal suggesting that transient knockdown of CHST15 is sufficient to alter 4,6-sulfation of CS-GAGs.
source: By 10 days after MI, CHST15 protein levels had returned to normal suggesting that transient knockdown of CHST15 is sufficient to alter 4,6-sulfation of CS-GAGs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing normal CHST15 levels but reduced sulfation at day 10.

claim: siChst15 knockdown led to increased NG2 core protein expression compared to non-targeting siRNA control.
source: Interestingly, siChst15 knockdown led to increased NG2 core protein expression compared to non-targeting siRNA control (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6C with statistical analysis.

claim: The sympathetic neuron marker Tyrosine Hydroxylase (TH) was increased significantly in cardiac scar tissue from siChst15-treated animals compared to non-targeting siRNA control animals.
source: The sympathetic neuron marker Tyrosine Hydroxylase (TH) was increased significantly in cardiac scar tissue from siChst15-treated animals compared to non-targeting siRNA control animals (Figure 6D), suggesting successful sympathetic reinnervation of the cardiac scar.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6D with statistical analysis.

claim: Animals treated with an siRNA targeting Chst15 had restored TH-positive fibers in the infarct.
source: Animals treated with an siRNA targeting Chst15 had restored TH-positive fibers in the infarct (Figure 7C) at the same innervation density as the peri-infarct region (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: TH innervation density was significantly higher in the infarct of Chst15-targeted animals compared to non-targeting siRNA-treated animals.
source: TH innervation density was significantly higher in the infarct of Chst15-targeted animals compared to non-targeting siRNA-treated animals (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7E with statistical analysis.

claim: Cardiac scar size was not significantly different between Chst15 siRNA-treated and non-targeting siRNA-treated groups.
source: Cardiac scar size was examined between the two groups and no significant difference existed (Figure 7G and H).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 7G and H with statistical analysis.

claim: Restoration of nerves with Chst15 siRNA treatment reduced arrhythmias when compared to non-targeting siRNA control-treated animals.
source: To examine whether restoration of nerves reduced arrhythmia susceptibility, we examined arrhythmias by ECG after administration of the β-agonist isoproterenol and caffeine (Gardner et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2014). Restoration of nerves with Chst15 siRNA treatment reduced arrhythmias when compared to non-targeting siRNA control-treated animals (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is supported by arrhythmia scoring data shown in Figure 7F with statistical analysis.

claim: Reducing 4,6-tandem sulfated CS-GAGs in the cardiac scar after MI promotes sympathetic nerve regeneration back into the cardiac scar and reduces arrhythmia susceptibility after MI.
source: These results indicate that reducing 4,6-tandem sulfated CS-GAGs in the cardiac scar after MI promotes sympathetic nerve regeneration back into the cardiac scar and reduces arrhythmia susceptibility after MI.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the experimental results with siChst15 treatment.

claim: The CSPGs present in the cardiac scar after ischemia-reperfusion were enriched with sulfation at the 4 and 6 positions of CS-GAGs, which is often referred to as chondroitin sulfate E (CS-E).
source: This study investigated the role of CS-GAG side chain sulfation in preventing sympathetic axon regeneration in the heart after MI. We found that the CSPGs present in the cardiac scar after ischemia-reperfusion were enriched with sulfation at the 4 and 6 positions of CS-GAGs, which is often referred to as chondroitin sulfate E (CS-E) (Miller and Hsieh-Wilson, 2015).
evidence: This is a summary of findings supported by data and a citation for the nomenclature.

claim: CS-E inhibits the outgrowth of several types of neurons in the CNS.
source: CS-E inhibits the outgrowth of several types of neurons in the CNS (Brown et al., 2012; Gilbert et al., 2005), and our data indicate that it also prevents growth of sympathetic axons, since decreasing either 4S or 6S allowed axon regeneration.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: CS-E prevents growth of sympathetic axons, since decreasing either 4S or 6S allowed axon regeneration.
source: CS-E inhibits the outgrowth of several types of neurons in the CNS (Brown et al., 2012; Gilbert et al., 2005), and our data indicate that it also prevents growth of sympathetic axons, since decreasing either 4S or 6S allowed axon regeneration.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results showing that reducing sulfation allows axon regeneration.

claim: Nerve regeneration was confirmed by histology and by expression of the neuronal protein TH in cardiac scar tissue.
source: Nerve regeneration was confirmed by histology and by expression of the neuronal protein TH in cardiac scar tissue.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry and western blot data shown in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: Reinnervation throughout the left ventricle decreased isoproterenol-induced arrhythmias, consistent with previous studies targeting the neuronal CSPG receptor PTPσ.
source: Reinnervation throughout the left ventricle decreased isoproterenol-induced arrhythmias, consistent with previous studies targeting the neuronal CSPG receptor PTPσ (Gardner et al., 2015; Sepe et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by the arrhythmia data and citations to previous studies.

claim: Therapeutics targeting PTPσ to restore innervation shift the inflammatory response toward a more reparative phenotype, and in some cases decrease infarct size.
source: In addition, therapeutics targeting PTPσ to restore innervation shift the inflammatory response toward a more reparative phenotype, and in some cases decrease infarct size (Sepe et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Targeting CSPGs in the scar to restore innervation decreases arrhythmia susceptibility without altering infarct size.
source: These new data show that targeting CSPGs in the scar to restore innervation decreases arrhythmia susceptibility without altering infarct size.
evidence: This is supported by the arrhythmia and infarct size data from the siChst15 experiments.

claim: The core protein NG2 is an important source of CSPGs in the cardiac scar.
source: The core protein NG2 is an important source of CSPGs in the cardiac scar (Tian et al., 2014), and there is evidence that the NG2 core protein can inhibit sensory neurite extension independent of CS sulfation in certain contexts (Dou and Levine, 1994; Ughrin et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: There is evidence that the NG2 core protein can inhibit sensory neurite extension independent of CS sulfation in certain contexts.
source: The core protein NG2 is an important source of CSPGs in the cardiac scar (Tian et al., 2014), and there is evidence that the NG2 core protein can inhibit sensory neurite extension independent of CS sulfation in certain contexts (Dou and Levine, 1994; Ughrin et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Removing or preventing sulfation of CS-GAG chains was sufficient to allow axon regeneration into the cardiac scar.
source: While our data indicate that NG2 expression increases following MI, we found that removing or preventing sulfation of CS-GAG chains was sufficient to allow axon regeneration into the cardiac scar.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: NG2 prevents sympathetic axon regeneration in the heart exclusively through 4,6-tandem sulfation of CS side chains.
source: Thus, NG2 prevents sympathetic axon regeneration in the heart exclusively through 4,6-tandem sulfation of CS side chains.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the finding that removing sulfation allows regeneration despite NG2 presence.

claim: Increased 4,6-sulfation of CS-GAGs coincided with increased expression of the 4S-dependent 6-sulfotransferase CHST15.
source: Increased 4,6-sulfation of CS-GAGs coincided with increased expression of the 4S-dependent 6-sulfotransferase CHST15, which is the final enzyme in the production of CS-E, and depletion of the sulfatase ARSB which removes 4S.
evidence: This is supported by the temporal correlation of enzyme and sulfation changes shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: CHST15 is the final enzyme in the production of CS-E.
source: Increased 4,6-sulfation of CS-GAGs coincided with increased expression of the 4S-dependent 6-sulfotransferase CHST15, which is the final enzyme in the production of CS-E, and depletion of the sulfatase ARSB which removes 4S.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about CHST15 function.

claim: Changes in enzyme expression provide a potential mechanism for the shift to highly sulfated GAG side chains after MI.
source: These changes in enzyme expression provide a potential mechanism for the shift to highly sulfated GAG side chains after MI.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the correlation of enzyme expression changes and sulfation changes.

claim: Regulation of CHST15 and ARSB proteins is linked in the context of TBI and other diseases with a downregulation of ARSB leading to increased CHST15.
source: Regulation of these proteins is also linked in the context of TBI and other diseases with a downregulation of ARSB leading to increased CHST15 (Bhattacharyya et al., 2020 ; Bhattacharyya et al., 2017; Bhattacharyya et al., 2014; Bhattacharyya et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Hypoxia reduces ARSB activity, increasing the abundance of 4-sulfated CS-GAGs which enables Galectin-3 mediation of transcriptional changes.
source: Hypoxia reduces ARSB activity, increasing the abundance of 4-sulfated CS-GAGs which enables Galectin-3 mediation of transcriptional changes (Bhattacharyya et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Galectin-3 increased before changes were observed in expression of sulfation-related enzymes.
source: To our surprise, we found that Galectin-3 increased before changes were observed expression of sulfation-related enzymes.
evidence: This is supported by the temporal data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Increased Galectin-3 may be an early driver of the accumulating highly sulfated CS-GAGs observed by day 7 post-MI.
source: This suggests that increased Galectin-3 may be an early driver of the accumulating highly sulfated CS-GAGs observed by day 7 post-MI.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the temporal relationship of Galectin-3 increase and subsequent sulfation changes.

claim: At least one group has generated a novel small molecule to inhibit CHST15 and promote nerve growth.
source: The inhibitory effects of CS-E on axon outgrowth in certain neuronal subtypes led many to hypothesize that reducing CHST15 activity would restore nerve growth across CSPGs (Brown et al., 2012). To that end at least one group has even generated a novel small molecule to inhibit CHST15 and promote nerve growth (Cheung et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: siRNA knockdown of chst15 reduced CS-E in a colitis study in mouse.
source: We were inspired to test chst15 siRNA by a colitis study in mouse showing that siRNA knockdown of chst15 reduced CS-E (Suzuki et al., 2016; Suzuki et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Chst15 siRNA has been tested in a Phase 1 Clinical trial for Crohn's disease patients with active mucosal lesions.
source: More importantly, Chst15 siRNA has been tested in a Phase 1 Clinical trial for Crohn's disease patients with active mucosal lesions, and a Phase I/IIa trial for patients with pancreatic cancer (Tsuchiya et al., 2021), and has a good safety profile (Suzuki et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Chst15 siRNA has been tested in a Phase I/IIa trial for patients with pancreatic cancer.
source: More importantly, Chst15 siRNA has been tested in a Phase 1 Clinical trial for Crohn's disease patients with active mucosal lesions, and a Phase I/IIa trial for patients with pancreatic cancer (Tsuchiya et al., 2021), and has a good safety profile (Suzuki et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Chst15 siRNA has a good safety profile.
source: More importantly, Chst15 siRNA has been tested in a Phase 1 Clinical trial for Crohn's disease patients with active mucosal lesions, and a Phase I/IIa trial for patients with pancreatic cancer (Tsuchiya et al., 2021), and has a good safety profile (Suzuki et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: siRNA knockdown of Chst15 is potentially translatable to large animals and eventually human studies.
source: Thus, siRNA knockdown of Chst15 is potentially translatable to large animals and eventually human studies.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the clinical trial data.

claim: Three days after the last siRNA injection, CHST15 levels were similar in non-targeting siRNA and Chst15 siRNA hearts despite a significant reduction in 6S and reinnervation of the infarct in Chst15 siRNA-treated animals.
source: Three days after the last siRNA injection, CHST15 levels were similar in non-targeting siRNA and Chst15 siRNA hearts despite a significant reduction in 6S and reinnervation of the infarct in Chst15 siRNA-treated animals.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D,E and Figure 6A.

claim: A transient decrease in CHST15 protein and depletion of CS-GAG sulfation is sufficient to allow nerve restoration in the cardiac scar where NGF is abundant.
source: These data indicate that a transient decrease in CHST15 protein and depletion of CS-GAG sulfation is sufficient to allow nerve restoration in the cardiac scar where NGF is abundant.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the finding that transient knockdown leads to lasting reinnervation.

claim: ARSB is an FDA-approved therapeutic (Naglazyme) to treat mucopolysaccharidosis IV disease.
source: ARSB is an FDA-approved therapeutic (Naglazyme) to treat mucopolysaccharidosis IV disease (Harmatz et al., 2005; Harmatz et al., 2004; Muñoz-Rojas et al., 2010), which may be of use in the therapeutic context of the post-MI heart.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ARSB may be of use in the therapeutic context of the post-MI heart.
source: ARSB is an FDA-approved therapeutic (Naglazyme) to treat mucopolysaccharidosis IV disease (Harmatz et al., 2005; Harmatz et al., 2004; Muñoz-Rojas et al., 2010), which may be of use in the therapeutic context of the post-MI heart.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic application.

claim: This work demonstrates the critical nature of 4,6-sulfation of CS-GAGs in preventing reinnervation of the heart after MI.
source: Ultimately this work demonstrates the critical nature of 4,6-sulfation of CS-GAGs in preventing reinnervation of the heart after MI and provides two strategies to promote reinnervation by modulating CSPG sulfation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from all the experimental results.

claim: This work provides two strategies to promote reinnervation by modulating CSPG sulfation.
source: Ultimately this work demonstrates the critical nature of 4,6-sulfation of CS-GAGs in preventing reinnervation of the heart after MI and provides two strategies to promote reinnervation by modulating CSPG sulfation.
evidence: This refers to the ARSB enzyme treatment and siRNA knockdown of Chst15 demonstrated in the study.

claim: Modulating CSPG-sulfation after MI may be a therapeutic target to promote sympathetic nerve regeneration in the cardiac scar and reduce post-MI cardiac arrhythmias.
source: Our results suggest that modulating CSPG-sulfation after MI may be a therapeutic target to promote sympathetic nerve regeneration in the cardiac scar and reduce post-MI cardiac arrhythmias.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion about potential therapeutic applications based on the study results.

claim: SCG contain a relatively small number of cardiac sympathetic neurons.
source: Although SCG contain a relatively small number of cardiac sympathetic neurons, they provide a well-characterized model for axon outgrowth studies (Gardner and Habecker, 2013).
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about SCG.

claim: SCG provide a well-characterized model for axon outgrowth studies.
source: Although SCG contain a relatively small number of cardiac sympathetic neurons, they provide a well-characterized model for axon outgrowth studies (Gardner and Habecker, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Day 14 represents a time point when scar tissue is relatively stable and sympathetic nerves are excluded from entering the scar.
source: Day 14 represents a time point when scar tissue is relatively stable and sympathetic nerves are excluded from entering the scar.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about the MI model.

claim: NE was not increased with reinnervation, consistent with previous studies showing suppression of NE synthesis and reuptake by inflammatory cytokines.
source: NE content in the cardiac scar following siRNA treatment. NE was not increased with reinnervation, consistent with previous studies showing suppression of NE synthesis and reuptake by inflammatory cytokines (Parrish et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by HPLC data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1F and a citation to previous work.

claim: Reinnervation of borderzone myocytes may play an important role in decreasing arrhythmia susceptibility.
source: We do not fully understand the mechanisms by which reinnervation decreases arrhythmia susceptibility, but reinnervation of borderzone myocytes may play an important role.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential mechanisms.

claim: It remains unknown if modulating CSPG sulfation alters the inflammatory response.
source: It remains unknown if modulating CSPG sulfation alters the inflammatory response.
evidence: This is an explicit statement about a knowledge gap.
